# zapline

> zapline is a fast, batteries-included Rust web framework: FastAPI-style typed handlers, OpenAPI 3.1 generated from code, validation, DI, auth, sessions, WebSockets, metrics and a thread-per-core server. One prelude (`use zapline::prelude::*`), route macros, `App::new().mount(..).run(addr)`, and an in-process test client (`app.test()`).

Conventions an assistant should follow: handlers are `async fn` with extractor arguments (`Path`, `Query`, `Json`, `Valid<Json<T>>`, `State`, `Dep`); errors are `zapline::Result<T>` with `Error::not_found()` and friends plus `.with_code("snake_case")`; no `#[tokio::main]` (`App::run` owns the runtime); middleware is `async fn(Request, Next) -> Response`.

- [Cheatsheet](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/cheatsheet.html): start here; one runnable file with the canonical way to do each common task (~3k tokens)
- [Whole guide as one file](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/llms-full.txt): every page below, concatenated
- [API reference](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/api/zapline/): rustdoc for the `zapline` crate
- [Source](https://github.com/samsamurai301/zapline)

## Core concepts

- [Routing](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/routing.html): There are three equivalent styles. Use whichever reads best.
- [Extractors](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/extractors.html): Handler arguments are *extractors*: types that know how to build themselves from the request. A handler can take up to 12 arguments. Every argument except the l
- [Responses](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/responses.html): A handler can return anything that implements `IntoResponse`:
- [Errors](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/errors.html): zapline has one error type, `zapline::Error`, and one result alias, `zapline::Result<T>`.
- [Middleware](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/middleware.html): Middleware is an async function that receives the request plus `next`, the rest of the pipeline:
- [State, lifecycle & plugins](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/lifecycle.html): Register any `Clone + Send + Sync + 'static` value and extract it with `State<T>`:
- [Testing](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/testing.html): `App::test()` turns an app into an in-process client. It runs the full pipeline (global middleware, routing, route middleware, extractors, handlers, error rende

## Building APIs

- [OpenAPI & interactive docs](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/openapi.html): Add one line, and your API documents itself: an OpenAPI 3.1 spec at `/openapi.json` plus Swagger UI at `/docs`.
- [Validation](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/validation.html): Wrap an extractor in `Valid` and derive `Validate` on the type. Bad input never reaches your handler.
- [Dependency injection](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/di.html): Register a service once with `App::provide`, receive it in any handler with `Dep<T>`:
- [Configuration](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/config.html): Load layered settings into your own struct, then hand it to the app:
- [Background tasks & scheduled jobs](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/tasks.html): Queue work from a handler with `BackgroundTasks`, run periodic jobs with `App::schedule`, and run long-lived workers with `App::background`. All three are stopp

## Full-stack

- [Databases (Postgres, SQLite)](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/database.html): `zapline::db` connects your app to Postgres or SQLite through [sqlx](https://docs.rs/sqlx): a connection pool created at startup, SQL migrations applied automat
- [Views & htmx](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/views.html): `zapline::view` (feature `views`) renders HTML with [MiniJinja](https://docs.rs/minijinja) templates (Jinja2 syntax: `{{ value }}`, `{% for %}`, `{% extends %}`
- [Durable jobs](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/jobs.html): Work that must not be lost (emails, webhooks, image processing, billing) goes in a **job**: a struct stored in your database until a worker has run it. Jobs sur
- [Email](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/mail.html): `zapline::mail` sends email over SMTP in production, keeps it in a **dev inbox** you can open in the browser while developing, and captures it in tests.

- [Hardening middleware](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/hardening.html): A handful of built-in middleware turn a working service into one you can put on the internet. Each is one line:

- [Feature flags](https://samsamurai301.github.io/zapline/features.html): zapline follows "pay only for what you use": anything that pulls in a dependency sits behind a Cargo feature, and a feature you don't use adds no code to your b
